# 00.0 Welcome to HTML

Open any website — a social feed, a news article, an online store, a personal blog — and underneath what you see is the same foundation: **HTML** (HyperText Markup Language). It is the language that defines the structure and meaning of web content. Think of it as the blueprint of a building: it lays out what goes where, while other technologies decide how it looks (CSS) and how it behaves (JavaScript).

![/.learn/assets/chatgpt-image-feb-6-2026-10_38_51-am.png](/.learn/assets/chatgpt-image-feb-6-2026-10_38_51-am.png)

Because HTML describes structure and meaning, it is also what makes the web *work for everyone* — screen readers, search engines, and browsers all rely on well-formed HTML to understand a page. Get the structure right and everything built on top of it has a solid base.

This course is hands-on. You'll start from what HTML is and how the browser reads it, then build real pages: structuring text with headings, paragraphs, and lists; connecting pages with links and navigation; adding images, audio, and video; organizing content with semantic elements; writing clean, valid markup; and working responsibly with AI to generate HTML. Along the way you'll complete short coding challenges and a knowledge check.

By the end, you'll be able to build well-structured, accessible HTML documents from scratch. Let's start with the building blocks of the web.
